skill.name: remove-git-worktree
skill.description: Removes a Git worktree and its matching local branch after repository work is complete.
skill.summary: Clean up a named Git worktree and local branch.
skill.author: AKABANAKK

security_audit.summary: The skill is a small Bash helper for deleting a computed Git worktree and then force-deleting the matching local branch. Most static external-command hits are benign command substitutions or Markdown formatting, but the parent-directory path construction and destructive cleanup flow warrant review. No prompt-injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Worktree path is constructed outside the repository root.
remediation.suggestion: Canonicalize the target path, reject dot segments, and require it to remain under the expected worktrees directory before removal.

remediation.issue: Cleanup runs without confirmation or dry-run output.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit confirmation step and a dry-run mode that prints the worktree path and branch before deletion.

remediation.issue: Branch input is not validated before Git deletion commands.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the branch name with Git reference checks and use argument delimiters before branch names.

finding_verdicts.reason: This command substitution only transforms a quoted branch name by replacing slashes with hyphens. It does not evaluate the branch name as shell syntax, so no command injection is evident.
The command runs hardcoded git rev-parse to find the repository root. No user-controlled argument is passed to the command.
The command runs basename on a quoted repository path returned by Git. The value is not executed as code, and the command is ordinary path derivation.
The shebang identifies this as a Bash helper, but the shell invocation itself is not hidden or suspicious. Risk comes from later destructive operations, which are covered separately.

The deletion target is built with a parent-directory segment that moves outside the repository root before later removal. The branch component is only partially normalized, so the computed filesystem target should be validated before destructive use.
The flagged text is a Markdown code fence showing a usage command. It is documentation, not Ruby backtick execution.

content.value_statement: Old Git worktrees and branches can clutter local repositories after feature work. This skill runs a focused cleanup helper for a named branch.
actual_capabilities: Accepts a branch name as the cleanup target.
Builds the expected sibling worktree directory name.
Checks whether the computed worktree directory exists.
Runs Git worktree removal for the computed path.
Deletes the matching local branch when it exists.
limitations: Only supports repositories that use the expected sibling worktrees directory pattern.
Does not prompt for confirmation before removal.
Does not check remote branches or pull request status.
Requires Bash and Git on the local machine.

use_cases.title: Clean Finished Feature Branches
use_cases.description: Remove a local worktree after a feature branch has been merged or abandoned.

use_cases.title: Keep Worktree Folders Organized
use_cases.description: Clear stale sibling worktree directories that follow the repository naming convention.

use_cases.title: Automate Local Repository Cleanup
use_cases.description: Give an AI coding agent a repeatable cleanup command for known branch names.

prompt_templates.title: Remove One Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup for a known branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Remove the Git worktree for branch feature/example using this skill. Show the target branch before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Clean After Merge
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine cleanup after a merged branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to clean up the local worktree for my merged branch. Confirm the branch name with me first.

prompt_templates.title: Verify The Target Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Safer cleanup when the worktree path matters.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before removing the worktree, compute the expected path and ask me to confirm it matches my intended branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review Cleanup Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the branch name, explain what local data will be removed, then run the worktree cleanup only after approval.

output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the branch, displays the expected worktree path, removes the worktree, and deletes the local branch if present.

output_examples.input: Clean up the abandoned experiment branch.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for the exact branch name, checks the computed worktree location, and performs cleanup after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Remove a branch worktree from the wrong repository directory.
output_examples.output: The assistant warns that the command should run from the main repository and asks the user to switch directories first.

best_practices: Run from the main repository, not from an unrelated directory.
Confirm the branch has been merged or backed up before cleanup.
Review the printed worktree path before allowing removal.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for unknown branch names from untrusted text.
Do not run it when the worktree has uncommitted changes.
Do not assume it removes remote branches or pull requests.

faq.question: What does this skill remove?
faq.answer: It removes a computed local Git worktree and deletes the matching local branch when it exists.

faq.question: Does it delete remote branches?
faq.answer: No. It only targets local worktrees and local branches.

faq.question: Can I use it outside a Git repository?
faq.answer: No. It needs Git to identify the current repository root.

faq.question: Does it ask before deleting files?
faq.answer: No. The current script removes the worktree without an interactive confirmation step.

faq.question: Which worktree layout does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects sibling worktree folders that use the repository name followed by a worktrees suffix.

faq.question: Is it safe for unmerged branches?
faq.answer: Use caution. Confirm important commits are merged or backed up before removing a worktree or deleting a branch.
